6adde6bc3e27a32eac5daa57d30ab373f77690be.query: In the paper “Context-Aware Learning for Neural Machine Translation”, Is the proposed model more sensitive than previous context-aware models too?
6adde6bc3e27a32eac5daa57d30ab373f77690be.diagnosis: Unlike the opening of A, B limits the comparative claim to some prior studies. The authors explicitly make that comparison. Its qualification preserves a grounded answer.

short_witnesses_from_B.text: sensitive to the context, contrarily to some previous works

A.answer: Yes. The paper reports that the model trained with the proposed learning algorithm is more sensitive to additional context than previous context-aware models. Comparing performance with actual versus random contexts shows that the proposed training makes the model more sensitive to the additional context [1], and the authors state that the model is "indeed sensitive to the context, contrarily to some previous works" [3]. In contrast, a larger-context model trained only to maximize log-likelihood largely ignores the previous sentence, with translation quality degrading only marginally (ΔBLEU = 0.40) when an incorrectly paired previous sentence is supplied [5]. The conclusion likewise states that a larger-context model trained with the proposed approach becomes more sensitive to the additional context and outperforms a context-less baseline [2].

B.answer: Yes, but the evidence supports this specifically against “some previous works”: the paper states that the model trained with the proposed algorithm “is indeed sensitive to the context, contrarily to some previous works” [3][4], and the conclusion says the larger-context model trained by the proposed approach “becomes more sensitive to the additional context” [1]. The evidence does not provide a broad quantitative comparison showing it is more sensitive than all previous context-aware models.

short_witnesses_from_B.text: a framework for studying learned and engineered representations of text

A.answer: INFODENS provides exploration of both learned and engineered (hand-crafted) representations of text for text classification tasks. It is designed to simplify feature engineering and provide the groundwork for extracting learned features and combining both approaches [1]. The paper describes it as a framework aimed at studying hand-crafted and learned representations [3], and it enables rapid evaluation of different text representations on different tasks [2]. It also shows that combining hand-crafted and learned representations can be beneficial [2].

B.answer: INFODENS is a framework for studying learned and engineered representations of text in the context of text classification tasks [1]. It is designed to simplify feature engineering, provide the groundwork for extracting learned features, and support combining both approaches [1].
